Landscape Ontario Congress 2027: a crew owner's game plan

Landscape Ontario Congress 2027 runs Jan. 12-14 in Toronto. A crew owner's plan for suppliers, equipment, software demos and the week after.

The short answer

Landscape Ontario says its Congress Trade Show and Conference returns to the Toronto Congress Centre in Toronto on January 12-14, 2027, and that early-bird pricing ends December 15, 2026 (Landscape Ontario's save-the-date page). Confirm both there before you book. The plan: walk in with three decisions to settle, one real job on paper, and a follow-up list for the week after.

Online registration opened September 1, 2026, according to the same page. Ticket prices are not covered here. Check them when you register, and re-check the dates and the early-bird deadline on Landscape Ontario's own site, since event details can change. This is an independent guide.

Two more points from that page. Members of listed industry organizations (CFIA, CNLA, Landscape Ontario, OALA and OPA) can use the VIP code LO2027 for complimentary trade show admission, a $25 value. Codes and who qualifies can change, so check the page before you count on it. Landscape Ontario also says Congress attendee lists are never sold or rented, and it warns attendees about scam offers of attendee lists and hotel deals. If an email offers you either, check with Landscape Ontario directly before you pay anyone.

Before you go: bring three decisions

Three days on a show floor go fast. Walk the aisles without a list and you come home with a bag of brochures and a sore back. Pick the decisions you want settled before your first spring site walk, and write them on one page.

  • Price sheet: the ten or so materials that drive your quotes (pavers, base, edge restraint, polymeric sand, armour stone, sod, mulch) and what you paid for each this year.
  • Equipment: one machine or attachment you are deciding on, your crew-day cost, and a count of last season's jobs where it would have been used.
  • Software: one real job from this season, written up from first call to final invoice, to hand every vendor.
  • Also pack: business cards, a pen, a charged phone, and a folder for quotes so they don't end up in the truck door.

If one decision is enough this year, bring one. A settled decision is worth more than three half-answers.

Questions for suppliers about 2027 price sheets

Your 2027 quotes are only as good as the price sheet under them. Ask the same questions at every booth so you can line the answers up later. Write the answers on the back of each card before you leave the booth.

Swipe the table sideways to see every column.

Supplier questions to ask at every booth
AskWhy it matters for your quotes
When will your 2027 price sheet be final, and can you send it in writing?You need firm numbers before you quote spring jobs.
How long will a quoted price hold?A quote you send in March may not be accepted until May.
What are lead times on the colours and styles I use, in May and June?A late delivery moves your schedule and your crew.
What are the delivery minimums, fees and drop rules?Delivery belongs on your quote, not on your job as a surprise.
What is your return policy on full and broken pallets, and are there pallet deposits?Leftover material is either a credit or a cost on the job.
What happens when a colour is out of stock?You want the substitution answer before the homeowner picks a colour.

If you price interlock or patios, carry those answers straight into your numbers. How to price interlock and hardscape jobs for 2027 covers pricing interlock driveways and patios from your own costs.

Equipment: work it out in crew-days

A machine on a show floor always looks good. It is clean, it has a bow on it and the salesperson has a number ready. Your job is to turn that number into crew-days and dollars on your own jobs.

Example: Say your crew-day (four people, one truck) costs you $1,500 in labour. A dealer tells you a machine saves one crew-day of dig-out and base prep on a driveway. Last season you did 20 driveways. On paper that is 20 crew-days, or $30,000 of labour you could move to other work. Now set the machine's yearly cost against it: payments or lease, insurance, maintenance, fuel, a trailer, and the months it sits through winter. Then ask the harder question: do you have 20 more crew-days of work to put that time into, or will the crew just finish early? These numbers are illustrative; use your own.

Don't take the one-crew-day claim as given. Ask the dealer to show it on a job like yours, or rent the machine for a week in spring and time two driveways. Questions to ask at the booth:

  • Can it be delivered before your first spring job?
  • Is there a rental or rent-to-own option so you can test it first?
  • Where is service done, and is there a loaner if it goes down in June?
  • Which attachments do you need for your work, and what do they add?
  • What does the warranty cover, in writing?

Landscape Ontario lists the Electric Demo Area among the returning features for 2027 (Landscape Ontario's register-now page). Before you commit to a purchase, ask your accountant how it is treated for tax in your situation.

Software demos: bring one real job

Every software booth has a polished demo with a perfect sample customer. That tells you little. Hand each vendor the same real job from this season and ask them to run it while you watch, from lead to invoice.

  1. Enter the lead the way it came in: web form, phone call or referral.
  2. Build the quote from your site notes and your prices, line by line.
  3. Have the customer accept it, the way your customer would.
  4. Turn the accepted quote into an invoice with your deposit.
  5. Put the job on the schedule and get word to the crew.
  6. Show labour and material costs against the job.

Watch for retyping. Every time the same name, address or price gets keyed in twice, write it down. That is the work your office does at the kitchen table at 10 pm.

Then ask every vendor the same questions:

  • What is live today, and what is on the roadmap? Get that answer in writing.
  • Is it priced per user or at a flat price?
  • Who does the setup, and how long does it take?
  • What is the contract term?
  • Can you export all your data, and in what format?
  • Where is your data stored?

If a vendor can't run your job at the booth, book a follow-up where they can. A demo on your own job is the only one worth comparing.

Sessions and owner-to-owner conversations

Landscape Ontario describes the morning conference sessions as providing practical knowledge, business strategies, technical expertise and innovative solutions. Returning features for 2027 include the Electric Demo Area, the LIVE Stage education area, the Landscape Designers Conference, the LO Awards of Excellence Ceremony, the Hiring Party and the Women in Horticulture event, and some feature events may need an extra ticket (register-now page). The save-the-date page lists the Landscape Designers Conference on January 11, 2027 and the Awards of Excellence Ceremony on January 12, 2027.

If you are hiring for spring, put the Hiring Party on your list and check whether it needs a ticket. For sessions, pick the ones that match your three decisions and skip the rest.

The hallway can be as useful as the session room. Other owners are not your competition at a coffee table in January. Ask them specific questions: how they price a crew-day, which machine they would buy again, how they handle a rained-out week. Specific questions get specific answers.

The week after: a one-page follow-up list

The show is only worth the follow-up. Block a morning in the week after and work through this list while the notes still make sense.

  • Sort cards and notes into three piles: price sheet, equipment, software.
  • Ask each supplier for the final 2027 price sheet in writing, with the price-hold period and delivery terms.
  • Update your own price sheet before you send your first spring quote.
  • Get written quotes on the equipment you are deciding on, and book a rental test if the dealer offers one.
  • Shortlist two software vendors and book a follow-up demo where they run your real job.
  • Set a decision date for each pile, and put it in your calendar.
  • Throw out the brochures you will never read.

Questions, answered

When is Landscape Ontario Congress 2027?

Landscape Ontario says its Congress Trade Show and Conference runs January 12-14, 2027 at the Toronto Congress Centre in Toronto. It lists the Landscape Designers Conference on January 11, 2027 and the Awards of Excellence Ceremony on January 12, 2027. Event details can change, so confirm them on landscapeontario.com before you book.

Where is Landscape Ontario Congress held?

Landscape Ontario says Congress 2027 returns to the Toronto Congress Centre in Toronto, Ont. Check Landscape Ontario's own pages for the latest event details before you travel.

When does early-bird registration end for Congress 2027?

Landscape Ontario says early-bird pricing ends December 15, 2026. Online registration opened September 1, 2026. Ticket prices are not covered here; check them when you register, and re-check the deadline on landscapeontario.com.

What should a contractor bring to a trade show?

Bring the decisions you want settled before spring: your current price sheet with what you paid for key materials, your crew-day cost and a count of jobs for any equipment you are weighing, and one real job written up from first call to final invoice for software vendors. Add business cards, a pen, a charged phone and a folder for quotes.

How do I compare software vendors at a trade show?

Hand every vendor the same real job and ask them to run it from lead to invoice: enter the lead, build the quote from your notes, have the customer accept it, invoice the deposit, schedule the job and show costs against it. Note every time something gets retyped. Then ask each one what is live today versus on the roadmap, how pricing is structured, who does setup and how long it takes, the contract term, data export and where your data is stored.
